provenance.sourceName: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API — ECMWF ERA5 reanalysis (Copernicus Climate Change Service, C3S), daily precipitation_sum (models=era5)
provenance.geographicScope: 50 district anchors (Bangkok); one series per area id
provenance.methodology: Daily precipitation at each area anchor by inverse-distance weighting (power 2) of the 4 nearest points of the reanalysis lattice in rain-grid.json (distances in local metres; a lattice point closer than 1 m is used alone; null inputs are skipped and weights renormalised); rounded to 0.1 mm. The lattice values are ECMWF ERA5 reanalysis daily totals served by Open-Meteo (models=era5): Modelled reanalysis precipitation, NOT rain-gauge observations. Source: ECMWF ERA5 reanalysis (Copernicus Climate Change Service, C3S), 0.25° × 0.25° regular latitude/longitude grid (≈27–28 km), hourly, served by https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive with models=era5 (the same model for Bangkok and Hat Yai and for the whole period 2024-01-01..2026-10-28). Daily value = Open-Meteo daily precipitation_sum in local time (Asia/Bangkok, UTC+7) = sum of the 24 hourly values stamped 00:00–23:00, each the accumulation over the preceding hour, i.e. the window (D−1 23:00, D 23:00] local; rounded to 0.1 mm (mm/day). ERA5 cells are coarser than the 0.1° lattice: Open-Meteo answers every coordinate with one model cell (no interpolation), so the 42 lattice points carry the series of 11 distinct ERA5 cells and neighbouring points repeat identical values. Point-to-cell mapping was recorded with one short request covering all points (2024-09-01..2024-09-14); the full period was then fetched once per cell at the first point mapped to it, and all 42/42 points were verified to have values identical to their cell's series over that window. Mapping in data/staged/rain-grid-meta.json. models=era5 chosen over era5_land (returns no precipitation on Open-Meteo) and best_match (identical to ECMWF IFS operational analysis/forecast archive on the checked windows, i.e. not a reanalysis). Data CC BY 4.0 by Open-Meteo (attribution: “Weather data by Open-Meteo.com”); contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information.
limitations: ERA5 reanalysis cells are 0.25° (≈27–28 km): neighbouring areas mostly share the same cell(s), so rainfall differences between neighbouring areas are mostly NOT resolved — the IDW only smooths between cell values and adds no local detail.
Model reanalysis, not observations: ERA5 at 0.25° (≈27–28 km) smooths convective cloudbursts and typically understates gauge maxima, especially for intense local storms.
Spatial detail is limited to 11 ERA5 cells; the 0.1° lattice does not add information beyond the cell boundaries.
Local-midnight daily boundaries (effectively 23:00–23:00 local) differ from TMD's 07:00–07:00 climatological day; do not compare day-by-day with TMD daily totals without accounting for this.
Period ends 2026-10-28 (latest complete ERA5 day available when retrieved, ~5-day latency); recent months are preliminary ERA5T and may be revised by C3S.
Free Open-Meteo API: non-commercial use only; attribution required (CC BY 4.0).
